## Objective
This is to calculate the sample size for the "pathologist_grading_set" - intended for comparing lymphocyte distribution grades (by pathologists) with AI-derived lymphocyte distribution features. 

Data on percentages, and ANOVA effect size for pathologists grade (majority opinion) vs normalized lymphocyte count (per wsi) from the paper "AI-based quantification of lymphocytes in feline small intestine" (Wulcan et al 2024, https://doi.org/10.1177/0300985824128682) is used for estimating prevalence of different grades and effect size. This should be conservative, since the intended analysis will have a higher spatial granularity.

## Rationale
Grade is a qualitative metric on a four grade scale (normal, mild, moderate, marked)
and mean distance to closest neighbor is quantitative. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) 
can be used to determine if the variance between groups is significantly larger than
the variance within groups. 
With just one categorical variable (but four levels), a one-way many groups anova is appropriate.
I do not expect the distance to nearest neighbor values to be normally distributed.
As a rough rule of thumb, if the groups are 2-9 the sample size for each group should be at least 15. 
The effect size for an AN
To calculate number of observations per group, this requires number of groups (k, 4),  effect size (Cohens f), signigicance level and power.


## Calculate effect size based on "AI-based quantificiation of lymphocytes paper"
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(effectsize)
library(pwr)
library(jsonlite)

#Read in data from previous paper 
grade_vs_density <- readRDS("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/Projects/AI/paper/AIFeBx_supplemental/test_analysis/output/wsiAI_vs_path/WSI_validationData.rds") %>%
  select(slide_name, median_grade, class_label, density_1000um2_median)

# Calculate effect size for previous sample
cohen_f_results <- grade_vs_density %>%
  group_by(class_label) %>%
  do({
    model <- aov(density_1000um2_median ~ as.factor(median_grade), data = .)
    #print(summary(model))
    f_val <- cohens_f(model, partial = FALSE)
    #print(f_val)
    data.frame(cohen_f = f_val$Cohens_f[1])
  })

# Calculate number of observations needed for new group using the lower of the two
effect_size <- min(cohen_f_results$cohen_f)     # Cohen's f
k <- 4                  # Number of groups
alpha <- 0.05
power <- 0.80

# Sample size calculation
power_anova <- pwr.anova.test(k = k, f = effect_size, sig.level = alpha, power = power)

n_per_grade <- power_anova$n

#Calculate frequency of grades 
grade_percentage <- grade_vs_density %>%
  group_by(class_label, median_grade) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  group_by(class_label) %>%
  mutate(percentage = count / sum(count) * 100)

lowest_grade_prevalence <- min(grade_percentage$percentage)

total_n <- (n_per_grade / lowest_grade_prevalence) * 100

print(total_n)
```

### Random sample from all scanned images
Sample 105 images (not more than one per bx_id and vmacs_patient_id)
Exclude any images used for training/tuning of models used in the paper, only use H&E stained. 
Sample size calculation 89, (estimate 85% retainment after excluding low quality slides (estimated in labl_2020_tuning set - 105 wsis for this should account for it)
```{r sample}
library(dplyr)

set.seed(12)

#Use image_index with duplicate slides removed
image_index_deduplicated <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/Projects/fe_si_images/output/index/image_index_deduplicated_2025-05-16.json")

#Only used H&E stained images
image_index_he <- image_index_deduplicated %>%
  filter(staining == "he") 

#Remove any images used for AI model development (training/tuning)
image_index_development_slides_removed <- image_index_he %>%
  filter(is.na(use_set_labl_2020) | use_set_labl_2020 == "test")

#Only one slide per biopsy id
# Randomly select one row per bx_id
no_dup_bx <- image_index_development_slides_removed %>%
  group_by(bx_id) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Only one slide per patient id (for vmacs cases)
has_pid <- no_dup_bx %>% filter(!is.na(vmacs_patient_id))
no_pid  <- no_dup_bx %>% filter(is.na(vmacs_patient_id))

# Randomly select one row per non-NA vmacs_patient_id
has_pid_unique <- has_pid %>%
  group_by(vmacs_patient_id) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Combine and sample 90
candidates <- bind_rows(has_pid_unique, no_pid)

sampled_images <- candidates %>% sample_n(105)

write_json(sampled_images, "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/Projects/fe_si_papers/spatial_lc_clustering/output/grading_sample/grading_sample.json", pretty = TRUE)


```

### Sample mucosal fragments from included images
For this chunk, one mucosal fragment for each included image is sampled.
The images are first processed with the model "fragments" to identify tissue fraggments and classify them as original or dulicates (to remove duplicate sections), the output fragments are manually reviewed by jmw (at low magnificaiton) to exclude fragments without small intestine, with mucosa destructive lesions or with MALT. The manually reviewed fragments are then classified with the model mucosa - to isolate regions of small intestinal mucosa, and classify them based on orientation and artefact. After exclusion of mucosal segments with inadequate orientation or artefact, and mucosal segments < 500,000 um2  one mucosal segments per wsi is randomly selected.
```{r}
library(jsonlite)
library(tidyverse)

set.seed(62)

mucosa_metadata_grading_sample <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_models/mucosa/output/mucosa/mucosa_metadata_grading_sample.json")  %>% #n 1408 - contains copies
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%  #820 duplicates removed
  ungroup()

quality_mucosa <- mucosa_metadata_grading_sample %>%
  group_by(image_name) %>% 
  filter(area_1000_um2 >500) %>% #596 small removed
  filter(orientation_class == "adequate" | orientation_class == "marginal") %>% #432 inaequate orientaiton removed
  filter(artefact_class == "adequate" | artefact_class == "marginal") #225 inadequate quality removed

mucosa_metadata_grading_sample_one <- quality_mucosa %>% 
  group_by(image_name) %>%       
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%         
  ungroup()    

write_json(mucosa_metadata_grading_sample_one, "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/lymphocyte_distribution_patterns_in_feline_small_intestinal_biopsies/output/grading_sample/sampled_mucosa.json", pretty = TRUE)
```

### Extract tiffs for included mucosa
To provide pathologists with cropped wsis with just the mucosal segment of interest from each ws:
- a qupath project for just the WSIs of interest is created
- a txt file with image names are generated to for reading to qupath
- geojson for the mucosal segments of interest are copied to a specific folder
- tiffs (downsampled by 2 are extracted with qupath with a custom groovy script)
- the cropped tiffs are uploaded to aiforia for pathologist review

```{r}
#read_in_sample and add filename for associated geojson
sample <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/lymphocyte_distribution_patterns_in_feline_small_intestinal_biopsies/output/grading_sample/sampled_mucosa.json")  %>%
  mutate(file_name = paste(name, "mucosa.geojson", sep = "_"))

subset <- fromJSON("~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_images/output/process_subset/subset_grading_sample.json") %>% filter(image_name %in% sample$image_name)

file_paths <- subset$file_path

writeLines(file_paths, "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/lymphocyte_distribution_patterns_in_feline_small_intestinal_biopsies//output/grading_sample/sampled_mucosa_paths.txt")

## Copy samples mucosa outlines to separate folder (funcrtion from fe_si_images/select_subset/)

origin_folder <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_models/mucosa/output/mucosa/"
destination_folder <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/lymphocyte_distribution_patterns_in_feline_small_intestinal_biopsies/output/grading_sample/sampled_mucosa/"

file_names <- sample$file_name

copy_selected_files(origin_folder, destination_folder, file_names)

grading_sample_template <- sample %>% select(name) %>%
  mutate(lymphocyte_size = "", 
         lymphocyte_homogeneity = "",
         villi_epithelium_lymphocytes_cellularity= "",
         villi_epithelium_lymphocytes_clustering = "",
         villi_epithelium_lymphocytes_junctional_gradient = "",
         villi_lamina_propria_lymphocytes_cellularity = "",
         villi_lamina_propria_lymphocytes_patchy_infiltration = "",
         villi_lamina_propria_lymphocytes_junctiona_gradient = "",
         crypts_epithelium_lymphocytes_cellularity= "",
         crypts_epithelium_lymphocytes_clustering = "",
         crypts_epithelium_lymphocytes_junctional_gradient = "",
         crypts_lamina_propria_lymphocytes_cellularity = "",
         crypts_lamina_propria_lymphocytes_patchy_infiltration = "",
         crypts_lamina_propria_lymphocytes_junctional_gradient = "",) %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. extract *leading* digits (may be NA) - to arrange same order as aiforia
    num_prefix = str_extract(name, "^0*[0-9]+"),
    num_val    = as.numeric(num_prefix),          # numeric value of that prefix
    rest       = str_replace(name, "^0*[0-9]+", ""),
    rest       = tolower(rest)                    # case-insensitive alpha ordering
  ) %>% 
  arrange(
    is.na(num_val),   # numbers (FALSE) first, non-numbers (TRUE) after
    num_val,          # numeric order: 4 < 24
    rest,             # within same number, "otb" before "xyz"
    tolower(name)     # final tie-break (pure-letter group)
  ) %>% 
  select(-num_prefix, -num_val, -rest)     

write_xlsx(grading_sample_template, "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/judits_work_keller_lab/fe_si_papers/lymphocyte_distribution_patterns_in_feline_small_intestinal_biopsies/output/grading_sample/template_grading_sample.xlsx")
                       
```
